City Council Regular Meeting
Public Comment from the Audience
•
If you wish to address the City Council, please complete a Speaker Request Card, as it must be handed to the City Clerk before the start of the meeting.
•
The City Council will hear public comments on matters not listed on the agenda during the Public Comments from the Audience period.
•
Opportunity to address the City Council (on non-agenda items) is limited to 3 minutes per speaker.
•
The City Council will hear public comments on items listed on the agenda during discussion of the matter and prior to a vote.
Brown Act
Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain matters for consideration at a future City Council meeting.
Rules of Decorum
Persons attending the meeting shall observe rules of propriety, decorum, good conduct, and refrain from impertinent or slanderous remarks. Violation of this rule shall result in such persons being barred from further audience before the governing body. Pursuant to Gov. Code Sect. 54954.3(c), any person who engages in unlawful interference shall be removed from chambers.
Americans with Disabilities Act
In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in this meeting, please contact the City Clerk's office at least 48 hours prior to the meeting to allow the City to make reasonable arrangements to ensure accessibility to the meeting or service.
This agenda was posted 72 hours in advance of the meeting at the City Hall, 8838 E. Valley Boulevard, Rosemead; the L.A. County Library, Rosemead Branch, 8800 E. Valley Boulevard, Rosemead; and other locations pursuant to RMC Sec. 1.08.020. Any writings or documents provided to a majority of the Rosemead City Council regarding any item on this agenda will be made available for public inspection in the City Clerk's office during normal business hours.

C.
Second Reading and Adoption of Ordinance No. 1023 Adding Chapter 1.14 to the Municipal Code to Allow for Electronic and Paperless Filing of Fair Political Practices Commission (FPPC) Campaign Disclosure Statements
On October 8, 2024, the City Council held the first reading of Ordinance No. 1023, which adds Chapter 1.14 to the Municipal Code. This chapter allows for electronic and paperless filing of Fair Political Practices Commission Campaign Disclosure Statements. To streamline this process, the City Clerk’s Office will implement NetFile, an electronic filing system that enables online submission of various FPPC forms, including Forms 460, 470, 496, and 497, while also complying with Secretary of State requirements. In order for the City of Rosemead to accept electronically filed statements, the City Council must adopt an ordinance that approves the use of this online filing system. This ordinance will include a legislative finding that the system operates securely and effectively, ensuring it does not unduly burden filers.
Recommendation: That the City Council approve and adopt the second reading, by title only, of Ordinance No. 1023, entitled: AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF ROSEMEAD AMENDING MUNICIPAL CODE ADDING CHAPTER 1.14 TO TITLE 1 REGARDING ELECTRONIC AND PAPERLESS FILING OF FAIR POLITICAL PRACTICES COMMISSION CAMPAIGN DISCLOSURE STATEMENTS
Staff Report
D.
Memorandum of Understanding with the El Monte Union High School District for School Year 2024-2025 School Resource Deputy Funding
The El Monte Union High School District contracts with the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department for a Special Assignment Deputy that is assigned to Rosemead High School as a School Resource Deputy. Through an annual Agreement, the City of Rosemead shares the cost of the School Resource Deputy with the El Monte Union High School District for the hours the School Resource Deputy is assigned to Rosemead High School. The proposed Agreement between the City and the El Monte Union High School District is for the School Resource Deputy Program for the
2024-2025 school calendar year.
Recommendation: That the City Council take the following actions:
1.
Approve and authorize, and direct the City Manager to execute the Memorandum of Understanding with El Monte Union High School District for School Year 2024-2025 School Resource Deputy funding;
2.
Approve the proposed use of JAG Program funds for the School Resource Deputy; and
3.
Approve the City Manager to execute JAG Program related documents and amendments.
Staff Report
E.
Walnut Grove Avenue Street Light Installation Project No. 43009 - Award of Contract
As part of the City’s Fiscal Year 2022-23 Capital Improvement Program, the City Council approved the Walnut Grove Avenue Street Light Installation Project.
The project consists of furnishing and installation of solar powered street LED light fixtures with concrete poles, construction of pole foundations, anchor bolts, and all related appurtenances. The project is located on Walnut Grove Avenue from
Marshall Avenue to Valley Boulevard. Since the proposed lighting system is solar powered, the installation will not require installation of conduits within the roadway on Walnut Grove Avenue, therefore the proposed work will not conflict with the recent resurfacing of Walnut Grove Avenue. This project will also remove and replace existing deteriorated light fixtures along Valley Boulevard from
Rosemead Boulevard to Loma Avenue. The project is funded with Measure R with a total available construction budget of approximately $410,00.00. As a result of a comprehensive bid analysis to determine the apparent low bid, the bid submitted by Elecnor Belco Electric, Inc. in the amount of $619,256.00 was determined to be the lowest responsive bid.
Recommendation: That the City Council take the following actions:
1.
Approve the plans and specifications for the Walnut Grove Avenue Street Light Installation – Project No. 43009; and
2.
Authorize the City Manager to execute a contract with Elecnor Belco Electric, Inc., for the bid amount totaling $619,256.00. In addition, authorize an amount of $61,925.60 (10%) as a contingency to cover the cost of unforeseen construction expenses, for a total construction budget of $681,181.60 and amend the City’s Fiscal Year 2024-25 CIP Budget to appropriate additional funds in the amount of $272,000.00 in Measure R funding to increase the total available construction budget to $682,000 by adopting Resolution No. 2024-57, entitled: A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF ROSEMEAD, CALIFORNIA, TO AMEND THE FISCAL YEAR 2024-25 CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT PROGRAM BUDGET AND APPROPRIATE ADDITIONAL FUNDS FOR THE WALNUT GROVE AVENUE STREET LIGHT INSTALLATION (PROJECT NO. 43009)
Staff Report
F.
Adopt Resolution No. 2024-58 - CalRecycle Revised Resolution Authorizing Submittal of Application(s) for all CalRecycle Grants for which City of Rosemead is Eligible
On October 8, 2024, the City Council adopted Resolution No. 2024-45 authorizing the submittal of applications to CalRecycle for all grants for which the City of Rosemead is eligible. The CalRecycle grant program allows the State of California to administer various grant programs in furtherance of the state efforts to reduce, recycle and reuse solid waste generated in the state, thereby preserving landfill capacity and protecting public health and safety and the environment. After submitting the new resolution to CalRecycle, their staff informed the City that Resolution No. 2024-45 would need to be revised to include specific language required of the grant program. Staff prepared a revised resolution to include the necessary language required for acceptance.
Recommendation: That the City Council adopt Resolution No. 2024-58, entitled: A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF ROSEMEAD, CALIFORNIA, AUTHORIZING SUBMITTAL OF APPLICATION(S) FOR ALL CALRECYCLE GRANTS FOR WHICH CITY OF ROSEMEAD IS ELIGIBLE
Staff Report
G.
Rosemead Park Restroom Renovation Adjacent to the Aquatic Center - Project No. 41026 – Award of Construction Contract
As part of the City’s Fiscal Year 2023-24 Capital Improvement Program, the City Council approved the Rosemead Park Restroom Renovation Project. The Project will renovate the existing men’s and women’s restrooms at Rosemead Park adjacent to the aquatic center. The Project scope includes upgrading deteriorating structures and inclusion of ADA compliant fixtures, installation of additional restroom stalls, interior surfacing, plumbing, and lighting modifications. On September 23, 2024, staff published a Notice Inviting Bids for construction of the Project. On October 23, 2024, the City received ten (10) bids. Based on staff’s comprehensive bid analysis, the bid submitted by Bridgerock Construction, Inc., in the amount of $258,800,
is determined to be the lowest responsive bid.
Recommendation: That the City Council take the following actions:
1.
Approve the plans and specifications for the Rosemead Park Restroom Renovation Adjacent to the Aquatic Center – Project No. 41026;
2.
Waive the minor irregularity in Bridgerock Construction, Inc’s bid; and
3.
Authorize the City Manager to execute a construction contract with Bridgerock Construction, Inc., in the amount of $258,800. In addition, authorize an amount of $25,880 (10%) as a contingency to cover the cost of unforeseen construction expenses, for a total construction budget of $284,680.
Staff Report
H.
Purchase of Annual Microsoft Office 365 Licensing and Microsoft Entra ID Premium 2 Licensing
In light of recent numerous incidents of ransomware and other security incidents targeting government entities, the City of Rosemead has a need to preserve its security posture relative to accessing City computers and business systems. After a thorough analysis of the options, the Information Technology Division believes the Microsoft Entra ID Premium 2 licensing provides the best value and functionality to meet the City’s security needs. The proposed quote is in the amount of $46,200 for the purchase of annual Microsoft Office 365 renewal licenses ($33,180) and Microsoft Entra ID Premium 2 renewal licenses ($13,020).
Recommendation: That the City Council authorize the City Manager to execute the purchase of the annual Microsoft Office 365 licensing and Microsoft Entra ID Premium 2 licensing with Microsoft via the authorized retailer Intelli-Tech in the amount of $46,200.
Staff Report
I.
Adoption of the 2024 City of Rosemead Local Hazard Mitigation Plan
The Disaster Mitigation Act of 2000 requires communities to develop, implement, and updates of a Local Hazard Mitigation Plan recognizing potential natural hazards and to identify and consider mitigation measures to reduce the risks associated with those hazards. The Local Hazard Mitigation Plan is a tool to aid in facility and infrastructure planning and improvements and is a requirement to qualify for federal hazard mitigation grants. The City’s current Hazard Mitigation Plan expired on
October 29, 2023. By law, a Local Hazard Mitigation Plan must be updated every five years and approved by the Federal Emergency Management Agency (“FEMA”), California Office of Emergency Services (“CalOES”), and adopted by the City Council. The adoption will be followed by FEMA’s Final Letter of Approval which will be added to the Final Plan.
Recommendation: That the City Council approve the 2024 Local Hazard Mitigation Plan, and authorize Emergency Planning Consultants to forward the resolution of approval to FEMA insurance of a Final Letter of Approval by adopting Resolution No. 2024-60, entitled: A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF ROSEMEAD, CALIFORNIA, ADOPTING THE 2024 LOCAL HAZARD MITIGATION PLAN IN ACCORDANCE WITH CALIFORNIA OFFICE OF EMERGENCY SERVICES (CALOES) AND FEDERAL EMERGENCY MANAGEMENT AGENCY (FEMA) REQUIREMENTS
Staff Report
J.
Award of Contract for Professional Information Technology Management Services
The City of Rosemead contracted information technology services with Max Power Technology, LLC in December 2019. Their contract is set to expire on
December 10, 2024. A competitive bid process was conducted, and eleven (11) qualified proposals were received. Based on a review of all proposals, staff is recommending the City Council authorize the City Manager to execute a
Professional Services Agreement with Acorn Technology Services for a 3-year contract in the amount of $431,820 through November 12, 2027, with the option for up to two one-year extensions.
Recommendation: That the City Council authorize the City Manager to execute a 3-year Professional Services Agreement in the amount of $431,820 through November 12, 2027, with Acorn Technology Services for Information Technology Management Services, including an option to renew for two one-year extensions.
Staff Report

K.
Receive and File the 1st Quarter Budget Report; Adoption of Resolution
No. 2024-62, Amending the FY 2024-25 Operating and Capital Improvement Program Budgets
The financial position of the City for the General Fund for FY 2023-24 (unaudited) and FY 2024-25 through September 30, 2024 (1st Quarter) is summarized in the report. Additionally, carryover appropriations for the Capital Improvement Program and suggested budget amendments are included. The actions proposed in the report include the adoption of Resolution No. 2024-62, which amends the FY 2024-25 Operating and Capital Improvement Program budgets. In summary, the data presented has shown that the actual revenue for the General Fund in FY 2024, exceeded the estimated budget by $1.2 million, while expenditures were $1.6 million lower than the budgeted appropriations. The General Fund's fund balance underwent a net increase of $2.0 million in Fiscal Year 2024, increasing from $32.4 million to $34.5 million. In addition, a total of $42.5 million in prior year appropriations across 14 funds will be carried forward to FY 2024-25 for 33 Capital Improvement Program projects. Additionally, the first quarter receipts for FY 2024-25 comprise 6.2% of the total revenue, which accounts for 25% of the year. Expenditures for the same period total 22%.
Recommendation: That the City Council take the following actions:
1.
Receive and file the 1st Quarter Budget Report;
2.
Adopt Resolution No. 2024-62, entitled: A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF ROSEMEAD, CALIFORNIA, AMENDING THE FY 2024-25 OPERATING BUDGET AND CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT PROGRAM BUDGETS
Staff Report
L.
Approval of Second Amendment to Interim City Engineer’s Employment Agreement as a Retired Annuitant Position
In May 2023, the City opened the recruitment for a permanent City Engineer due to the resignation of the previous City Engineer. On November 14, 2023, the City Council authorized the City Manager to appoint Mr. Albert Leung as a Retired Annuitant to the position of City Engineer as authorized per California Government Code Sections 7522.56 and 21221(h). The recruitment is ongoing, but the position remains vacant. Additionally, beginning August 12, 2024, the Director of Public Works position became vacant. On August 12, 2024, Mr. Leung became the Acting Director of Public Works until the position was filled on October 28, 2024. Therefore, staff is requesting an amendment to Mr. Albert Leung’s agreement for FY 2024-25 to include his Acting assignment and to allow for Acting Pay between
August 12, 2024, to October 27, 2024, and beginning October 28, 2024, Mr. Leung’s position and pay would revert back to City Engineer until such a time when the permanent City Engineer position is filled.
Recommendation: That the City Council approve and amend the Employment Agreement with Mr. Albert Leung to include time spent as Acting Director of Public Works and an increase in hourly rate appropriate to his acting assignment for the Retired Annuitant position per California Government Code Sections 7522.56 and 21221(h) by adopting Resolution No. 2024-59, entitled: A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF ROSEMEAD APPROVING THE SECOND AMENDMENT TO THE INTERIM CITY ENGINEER’S RETIRED ANNUITANT EMPLOYMENT AGREEMENT TO TEMPORARILY APPOINT ALBERT LEUNG AS ACTING PUBLIC WORKS DIRECTOR FROM THE PERIOD OF AUGUST 12th, 2024 THROUGH OCTOBER 27th, 2024
Staff Report
M.
City Hall Basement Level Interior Renovations Project No. 31027 - Award of Construction Contract
As part of the City’s Fiscal Year 2022-23 Capital Improvement Program Budget, the City Council approved the City Hall Basement Level Interior Renovations Project. The Project involves renovation including new paint, flooring, offices/cubicles, storage area, ceiling, lighting and renovations to the existing women’s and men’s restroom for ADA compliance. On September 24, 2024, staff published a Notice Inviting Bids for construction of the Project. On October 23, 2024, the City received seven (7) bids. Based on staff’s comprehensive bid analysis, the bid submitted by MLC Constructors in the amount of $1,367,825, is determined to be the lowest responsive bid.
Recommendation: That the City Council take the following actions:
1.
Approve the plans and specifications for the City Hall Basement Level Interior Renovations – Project No. 31027; and
2.
Authorize the City Manager to execute a construction contract with MLC Constructors, Inc. in the amount of $1,367,825. In addition, authorize an amount of $136,782.50 (10%) as a contingency to cover the cost of unforeseen construction expenses, for a total construction budget of $1,504,607.50 and amend the City’s Fiscal Year CIP Budget to appropriate additional funds in the amount of $704,607.50 in ARPA and Public Facilities funds to increase the total available construction budget to $1,504,607.50 by adopting Resolution
No. 2024-61 – entitled:
A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF ROSEMEAD, CALIFORNIA, TO AMEND THE FISCAL YEAR 2024-25 CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT PROGRAM BUDGET AND APPROPRIATE ADDITIONAL FUNDS FOR CITY HALL INTERIOR RENOVATIONS PROJECT NO. 31027
Staff Report
N.
Approve First Amendment to Services Agreement for Tree Maintenance Services with West Coast Arborists, Inc., Extending the Term to June 30, 2025 to Prepare and Release a New Request for Proposal, Conduct Job Walk, Prepare an Analysis of Proposals, Conduct City Council Meeting, and to Allow for Services Transition Period (If Needed)
On October 22, 2024, the City Council directed staff to reject all proposals received for Request for Proposal (RFP) No. 2024-24 for Tree Maintenance Services, update the RFP evaluation criteria and release a new RFP for Tree Maintenance Services, and authorized the City Manager to negotiate and enter an interim contract with West Coast Arborists (WCA). The City’s previous annual Tree Maintenance Service contract with WCA expired on September 10, 2024, and WCA had been providing services to the City under an interim contract that expired October 31, 2024. Staff is requesting an extension to the interim contract through June 30, 2025, to prepare and release a new RFP. Tree maintenance services in the scope of work for this contract includes tree trimming, service request trimming, tree removal and replacement, emergency response and the maintenance of a GIS based tree inventory. The City will continue with recommended grid trimming and initiate service requests on an as needed basis. Staff requests to increase the contract authority from $30,000 to $120,000 for continuity of tree trimming maintenance services through
June 30, 2025. WCA has agreed to maintain services under the same terms, conditions, and pricing through June 30, 2025.
Recommendation: That the City Council authorize the City Manager to execute the First Amendment to the Services Agreement with West Coast Arborists, Inc., to extend the term through June 30, 2025, and increase the contract compensation amount from $30,000 to $120,000.
Staff Report
O.
Adopt Resolution No. 2024-64 to Apply for and Accept Measure A Funds
The Safe, Clean Neighborhood Parks, Open Space Beaches, Rivers Protection, and Water Conservation Measure, or Measure A, was developed to meet current and future park needs throughout Los Angeles County. Its content reflects the findings of the Countywide Parks and Recreation Needs Assessment that was completed in 2016. Measure A was approved by voters in 2016 and includes both formula-based allocations to agencies throughout the study area, as well as competitive grants that are open to public agencies, non-profit organizations and schools. In order to apply for and accept Measure A funds, the Los Angeles County Regional Park and Open Space District requires a resolution from the City of Rosemead.
Recommendation: That the City Council adopt Resolution No. 2024-64, entitled: A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF ROSEMEAD, COUNTY OF LOS ANGELES, STATE OF CALIFORNIA, APPROVING THE BLANKET AUTHORITY TO FILE APPLICATIONS FOR GRANT FUNDS FROM THE LOS ANGELES COUNTY REGIONAL PARK AND OPEN SPACE DISTRICT FOR MEASURE A FUNDING FOR PROJECTS AND PROGRAMS
Staff Report
5.
MATTERS FROM CITY MANAGER & STAFF
A.
City of Rosemead Public Transit Services
On September 10, 2024, staff presented an analysis of current transit expenditures and ridership data, and a comparative analysis of implementing alternative
ride-hailing services. This report was provided in response to a request at the meeting on July 23, 2024, to gain a better understanding of current expenditures and explore options to enhance transportation services. In response to the September presentation, staff was asked to provide additional information to explore the feasibility of supplementing or replacing our current transit services with alternative options. The data is presented in several implementation matrices, which provide several options to explore the possibility of improving efficiency, availability, and cost of transit services in the City.
Recommendation: That the City Council receive and provide direction to staff.
Staff Report
6.
MATTERS FROM MAYOR & CITY COUNCIL
A.
Request to Agendize for a Future Meeting, Prohibiting Protest Activity in Residential Zones
At the request of Council Member Polly Low, she would like to discuss the possibility of agendizing for a future meeting an ordinance that would either prohibit or impose limitations on protest activities within residential zones.
Recommendation: That the City Council discuss and provide direction to City staff.
Staff Report
B.
Amendment to the Strategic Plan - Safety Response Times
At the request of Mayor Steven Ly, he would like to discuss and potentially take action on Strategic Plan 2030 – Goal A: Public Safety, specifically concerning response times.
Recommendation: That the City Council discuss and provide direction to City staff.
Staff Report
C.
Council Comments
